preview: Interview experience of Harsh Bhosale detailing an online coding round and three offline interview rounds including technical and HR discussions.
content: Interview Experience Harsh Bhosale Final year Electronics (2021-25) Criteria: 1. CPI: CGPA 7 or equivalent to 70% & above, no standing arrears 2. Class X: 70% and above 3. Class XII: 70% and above 4. Branches: CS, IT, Electrical, EXTC, Electronics. Rounds: 1. Online Coding Round 2. Technical Round – 1 (offline) 3. Technical Round – 2 (offline) 4. HR round (offline) Round 1: Online Coding round (120 mins) It was an online test on the Hackerrank Platform. It consisted of 4 sections Section 1: Coding problem. It was a leetcode hard problem based on bit manipulation named Minimum One Bit Operations to Make Integers Zero. Section 2: 20 MCQ on CS core subjects Section 3: 15 MCQ on general aptitude and communication 50 students were shortlisted. The general tip here is to complete the test with accurate solutions as early as possible because submission timing is also considered in online tests. Round 2: Technical Round 1 This round was scheduled on 5th August, 2024. Firstly, the PPT was presented and the interview began at 11 AM. Be attentive during PPT and ask relevant questions to catch attention. I was called for the interview. The interviewer greeted me and asked me to sit. Following are the questions he asked me, 1. Tell me about yourself Remember to frame the answer in such a way that you are guiding the interviewer to ask questions about the topics you have mentioned in the introduction. The introduction gives a direction for the interviewer to ask suitable questions and check how well-versed you are with the topics you mentioned. For example: I wanted him to ask me questions about C++, so at the end of the introduction, I mentioned that C++ is my primary programming language. 2. Then he asked whether I knew Java. I told him no. 3. He asked me to tell the difference between Java and C++. 4. Then he asked me what are the 4 pillars of OOPs, as I had mentioned OOPs in the previous answer. 5. He asked me to give a real-life example of inheritance and how is it useful. 6. Then he asked me to write a C++ code to find whether the given input character is alphabet or not. Remember to dry run through your solution before showing it to the interviewer. 7. Then he asked me to tell all data types in C++. 8. He asked me what is a stack data structure and can I create a stack data structure using an array. I explained to him what is a stack data structure and told him I can implement stack using classes and I can use an array or vector as a class data member. Moreover, for stack operations, I can write methods inside the class created. 9. He then asked me what operations we can perform on the stack and can I write the implementation for that operation in the stack class I’ve created. 10. He then asked me whether I knew sorting algorithms, and I said yes. So he asked me to code the implementation of the bubble sort algorithm. Also, mention the time and space complexity of your solution. 11. While looking through the solution he saw that I had used the swap STL function, so he asked me to write a code for swapping two variables without using a third variable. Remember this is one of the favorite questions of the interviewer, so practice it beforehand. 12. Then he asked me what is a view in SQL Oracle is a database company and you are expected to know SQL and DBMS well. So prepare well for these two topics, and before the interview just go through the top 50 interview questions for both the topics. He asked me whether I have any questions for him. I asked him what is his role and responsibility at OFSS. He explained it well. I then asked him one more question, Will my branch have any impact on my application? He began explaining that they only judge based on interview performance and the branch doesn’t matter to them. After coming out, within 5 minutes I was called for 2nd round. Round 3: Technical Round 2 My second round was scheduled with the vice president of OFSS. He asked me to wait outside, and then after 10 minutes, he called me inside. He looked at my resume and after looking at my surname he started conversing in Marathi. Throughout the interview, we spoke in Marathi. He asked me who took my round 1 and how was my performance there. So then he asked me that my branch is electronics and why I wanted to get into the IT industry. I told him from the first year, I wanted to get into IT industry but I wasn’t getting CS/IT branch in any Tier1-2 college in Mumbai. So he asked me my MHTCET percentile. Then he asked me about teaching and faculty quality at VJTI, he told me that this is not a tricky question so answer frankly. I told him older faculties teach their subjects very well but lately, the contract-based hiring system has started at VJTI, where I feel the quality is degrading. Then he asked me whether there is a need for change in the curriculum of engineering as you are taught 8085 microprocessors and currently, we have so much advancement in processors then what is the purpose of learning 8085? Then he asked me what I do on weekends, like what was my weekend schedule right from the first year. He then asked me other than academics and projects, what are the topics that I have an interest in. I told him I like to stay updated about geopolitics and I like to study Indian modern history apart from my academic subjects. He then asked me whether I knew what was happening in the world and Indian politics. He told me today the market has crashed and asked me whether I knew what is the reason behind it. I wasn’t aware of this part so I told no. So he gave me a hint it is related to Israel. So during that period, Israel killed one of the Hamas leaders in Iran. Later, He asked me whether I knew where is Israel and Iran on the world map. I luckily knew this. Then he asked me what Western countries were doing when we were fighting for independence. I told him in Western countries at that time Industrial Revolution was going on. Then he proceeded to ask me, Is the Kashmir situation getting better or worsening these days? He then asked me what is the permanent solution for countering terrorism in the Kashmir valley. Later our discussion moved to the exodus of Kashmiri pandits and then towards the beginning of the Kashmir issue which accounts for the Raja Hari Singh and Junagadh merger thing. He appreciated me for my awareness of how the Kashmir issue began. Then he asked me What is the most important thing that the world needs right now and how India can work on it. I told him about the semiconductor shortage thing and then told him that the world currently needs a lot of GPUs, so maybe we can work on it. He was not satisfied with it he told me there was something more. I told him we could work on the AIML part, that thing is currently booming. He told me not AIML it was GenAI that we should work on. He asked me which country has the most number of discoveries and innovations. I told him that US has the most number of patents so maybe it is US. Then he asked me to explain the LLM briefly. He asked me whether we students use chatGPT to submit our lab reports :/ Then he asked me why I think that we need developers as most of the part can be done using chatGPT. Finally, he asked me whether I wanted to ask him anything. I asked him about his responsibilities as a VP at Oracle. Then I asked him how he reached this position, like what was his journey. He explained this part for nearly 15 minutes. And at last, he told me that he had selected me from his end but there would be one more round which would be conducted by HR. Round 4: HR Round This was pretty much a chill round she just asked me whether I was eligible to work in India and whether I was ready to relocate. On the same day at 4:22, the results were announced and 12 candidates were selected. I was one of them. Tips: 1. Make sure you enter with a smile and greet them because your first impression can have a lot of impact. 2. Maintain a grooming standard in the interviews, because it impacts your body language. 3. Stay calm, and composed, and be confident because it matters a lot. 4. Prepare the “Tell me about yourself” and a few common HR questions beforehand and don’t try to mug them, just remember key points and tell the answer around it because most of the time we forget the answer that we have prepared. 5. For a DSA Question, try to think out loud and share your ideas with the interviewer. If the question is not clear to you, ask the interviewer to explain it again with some test case. 6. If you finished writing your code, make sure to dry-run it before presenting it to the interviewer. 7. When the interviewer is smiling, try to keep a smile on your face. When the interviewer is serious, do not appear nervous. 8. Try to give mock interviews before the actual one because it gives you so much confidence. 9. During your preparation when you are solving DSA problems try sometimes to explain that problem to yourself only it will help in interviews. And remember don’t directly jump to the optimal solution first tell the brute force solution and then optimize it. 10. Colour-print your resume on thick paper. It should look premium when the interviewer takes it in his hand. 11. Go through the top 50 interview questions for each subject before the interview. Most of the questions are asked from there itself. 12. I used to prepare anki deck for the DSA questions I practiced. So if you are starting your preparation early, try making decks for each topic and revise it from time to time. I’ve attached the link below for the decks I’ve created.
